card_pick.why: the one card presentation, a Safe CSS-3D pick: flip is BLOCKED (growth-vs-product), slide was the video before that (kcc20, 2026-10-22), cube is the least recently used safe pick (tao-detailed, 2026-10-17); the fresh picks book-flip and swap draw HTML into canvas and need the chrome canvas-draw-element render flag, never verified on this renderer, so they stay an open question for Mike. The cube's 3D turn pairs with the beveled-glass SPLIT panes that bring each card in and with the SPIN/Shake center spin on the verdict boards: one 3D language. Cards fire only at the four bed changes; each card exits by the cube into the chapter's first cover after its >= 1 s pause.

chapter_split_pick.why: Mike's Bear Markets cue: the SPLIT family (Swiftly Glass Blocks; the reference used 2-horizontal, 3-horizontal and corner-1-right-up) as the chapter / scene move, picked ONCE and used on EVERY chapter change: panes splitting horizontally in opposing directions read as the frame being pulled apart, the right move for a chapter break on a horror bed. At the four carded chapters it brings the card IN (the card then exits by the cube); at the three cardless chapters (3:35.3, 4:36.6, 5:32.7) it IS the chapter change. Where the chapter change is a FACE out (2:41.8, 5:32.7, 7:18.7, 9:07.3) the face-cut row carries this id: one move hides both edges. Run SILENT as the reference did; the card impact / the bed is the hit.

face_glitch_pick.why: the scary-adjacent face pick Mike set for this video (GLITCH, PROJECT-LOG 2026-10-25); the ledger's face_cut slot is advisory and film-burn was the previous video's, so Blocks is also the fresher of the two. With FACE STYLE glitch it rides the cut-OUTS only: every cover->face cut-IN is a random lib:split-swinging-offset-* id (ten cut-ins, ten different ids, long and short alternating), every punch point a random glitchoffset-* / blocks-* hit across the join.

face_leak_pick.why: NONE: FACE STYLE glitch (Mike 2026-10-16) replaces the light-leak punch with a glitch hit across the join; no punch-leak rows, no synthetic leak, the ledger's face_leak slot stays empty for this video.

scary_pick.subject: pumpkin
scary_pick.why: ONE subject per video: the pumpkin, because the two Bear Markets pumpkin plates (the fire act-break plate and scary-6 at Normal 75) are Mike's own cue and the stinger subject must match them. The pumpkin subject has one stinger id, so the stingers alternate scary-6 (screen, the change vanishes in the flash) and scary-6-normal75 (the footage dims to 40 %) and never repeat an id back to back. RESERVED: five stingers + the one fire plate in 10 minutes, the quiet house moves everywhere between them.

melt_pick.why: MELT/RGB is BLOCKED (growth-vs-product); MELT/Equidistant is the one other melt look and fits better anyway: the frame wrapping into swirling pole vortices is a surreal spatial collapse, the right texture for evidence liquefying into a verdict card in a horror video. Used only where a receipt / chart REFORMS into the risk card that carries its own figure (RL-1, RL-2, RL-6, RL-7, RL-8) and for the C35 thesis dial; full 0.84 s where the hold allows, short 0.44 s where under 3 s remain; direction varies by context (down for 'shrinking', up for its pair, roll for the dial).

spin_pick.why: FRESH in the ledger (never used); SPIN/Twirl is BLOCKED. A center spin that jitters with a baked camera-shake ride and lands rough and physical: the same handheld horror language as the two face shakes, and a 3D-ish turn that echoes the cube card. Used only where a receipt turns to a NEW FACET: the four contrarian / new-contender verdict boards (RL-3, RL-4, RL-5, RL-9); 1x full where the hold allows, 2x once on the creepiest chapter's landing, short where under 3 s remain, direction alternating.
